solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starving religious sect saved by US agent

indicators.note: something saved by another is held safe inside it, so the sect goes within the agent

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in American slang
the Amish are a Christian sect in Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A hungry Amish fugitive is sheltered by a sympathetic FBI man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone famished is extremely hungry, a straightforward synonym for starving.

clue.text: A very nice chap in rep

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a thoroughly decent fellow

explanation.surface: A charming man is acting in repertory theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' looks like repertory theatre, where the nice chap is performing; it is short for representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep, short for representative, acts for a company or person, as an agent does.

clue.text: Drunken parent I meet is in a drunken state

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger about, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inebriated mother or father I bump into is plainly sloshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperate means given to excess, especially in drinking alcohol, so a drunk person fits.

clue.text: Broadway musical interval section sent up Cats?

parts.note: a half is one section or part of a whole

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: cats are kept as pets

explanation.surface: A segment of the Broadway musical Cats is parodied during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadway' marks the American term: a half step is what the British call a semitone. 'Cats' looks like the show but is just pets.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a half step is the semitone, the smallest interval in Western music.

clue.text: You might say the ant I electrified needs treatment!

indicators.note: letters that need treatment are to be worked on and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A poor ant that I gave an electric shock requires medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'the' is the grammarian's definite article, so it is one example you might name.

clue.text: Server brought over one's drop with touch of arrogance

indicators.note: just a touch of the word means only its opening letter
brought over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
to sag is to drop or droop

explanation.surface: A tennis player's drop shot is delivered with a hint of arrogance.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi was a famous tennis player, and every tennis player serves, hence a server.

clue.text: A gun for every person

parts.note: piece is slang for a handgun

explanation.surface: A weapon is handed out to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means each, for every individual one.

clue.text: Detective losing head creates trouble

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a tail is a detective who follows a suspect

explanation.surface: A sleuth decapitated is bound to cause problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in 'what ails you?'

clue.text: Give the right letter-order for 'secure entrance'

parts.note: to spell a word is to give its letters in the correct order
to bind is to tie up, make secure

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to spell out the phrase 'secure entrance' correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as a noun, a doorway, but is the verb meaning to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to hold them enthralled, as if under a magic charm.

clue.text: Barter over books on the subject of choppers

indicators.note: one thing over another covers it, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: to deal is to trade or barter
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Haggling about books concerning helicopters, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppers' suggests helicopters or axes; here it is slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental means relating to teeth, which are jokingly called choppers.

clue.text: Spirited young gals pinching right fancy pants

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight between, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: fillies is a jocular term for lively young women

explanation.surface: Lively girls are shoplifting decorative underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' reads as stealing; it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frillies is informal for women's frilly underwear, so ornate knickers or pants.

clue.text: Tiny fragment gleaned from Nato message

indicators.note: gleaned from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scrap of intelligence picked up from a military alliance communique.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle of an element, so a minute fragment of anything.

clue.text: Temporary structure built on The Strand?

definitions.text: Temporary structure built on The Strand?

parts.words: Temporary structure built on The Strand
parts.note: a strand is a beach, where children build things the tide will wash away

explanation.surface: A pop-up building on London's famous street, the Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a major London street, which the capital letters steer you towards; a strand is also a shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Built of beach sand, this short-lived child's construction stands only until the tide comes in.

clue.text: Shadows house tiles cast over centre of patio

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are laid over the extra piece, enclosing it
letters cast are thrown about, landing in a new arrangement
the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: The roof tiles of a house throw shade across the middle of the patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges HOUSE TILES into SILHOUETES, and 'over' wraps it round T, the centre of 'patio'.
explanation.definitionFit: Silhouettes are dark outlines against light, which is what shadows are.

clue.text: Soldiers in HQ head to the sub- ground level

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the other letters

parts.note: a base is a headquarters

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: men is a common term for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops at headquarters make for the submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub-' looks like a submarine the soldiers are heading for, but it belongs to the definition: below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey of a building below ground.

clue.text: Everyone needs to support British team

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece is written below the other

parts.note: all means everyone
to lack is to need or be without

explanation.surface: A call for everyone to back a British side.
explanation.walkthrough: The All Blacks are New Zealand's rugby team, not British at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union side, famous for their black kit.

clue.text: One must charge boy that's made to lie

indicators.note: charging into something means rushing inside it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: lad means boy
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone has to accuse a youngster who's been forced to tell untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' looks like fibbing; it is lying down, as something laid has been made to lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past participle of lay, to put something down so that it rests.

clue.text: Cut the price of decorative cotton fabric?

parts.note: lace is an open decorative fabric, often of cotton
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A query about what ornamental textile is reduced to.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or wound flesh, so to cut.

clue.text: A little nipper in field chasing after fellow

indicators.note: the chasing piece follows the other one, so it comes second

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A small child in a meadow runs after a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little nipper' suggests a child; here it is something tiny that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a minute insect that bites, a small nipper in the literal sense.

clue.text: Articles by lawyer written about jailbird strangler

indicators.note: the outer letters are written about, around, the inner ones
one piece sits beside the next

parts.note: AN and A are the indefinite articles
a DA is a US district attorney
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: Pieces from a lawyer written about a prisoner who throttled victims.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaconda is a huge snake that kills its prey by squeezing it to death.

clue.text: Warnings about leader of troops in strong points

indicators.note: one word goes round, about, the other

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Alarms raised over a commander among fortified positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fore!' is the cry a golfer gives to warn people of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's fortes are the things they are best at, their strengths.

clue.text: Fly low? That requires courage!

parts.note: blue means sad, low in spirits
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: Flying low is a brave thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as a verb; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large blowfly with a metallic blue body.

clue.text: Golfer that hugs medium-sized trees

indicators.note: hugging something means wrapping round it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
M is the clothing abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A golf player who embraces trees of average height.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a tall deciduous tree, so elms are a group of them.

clue.text: Butch old lady seen at church by Oscar

parts.note: your old lady is informal for your mother, ma
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tough-looking mother spotted at church with a man called Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch and macho both describe aggressively masculine behaviour or appearance.

clue.text: A clue-type relying on structure: this illustrative clue primarily?

definitions.text: A clue-type relying on structure: this illustrative clue primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A description of a clue type built on its arrangement, with this clue offered as the example.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is its own example: its initials spell out the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a composition whose initial letters spell a word, the form this very clue takes.

clue.text: After cutting away top, fashion creative work

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: A designer trims the top and produces an original piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, a piece of creative writing.

clue.text: Go for a riding harness one's heard of on radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; tack is the saddle and bridle of a horse

explanation.surface: Going in search of horse gear someone heard advertised on the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is to set upon them, to assault them.

clue.text: Estimate cost of donkeys eating last of crops

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so a letter goes within

parts.note: asses are donkeys

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Pricing the damage when donkeys munch the end of the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to evaluate it, for instance its value for tax.

clue.text: One stopping US philosopher coming out

indicators.note: a stopping plugs a hole, so the letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American philosopher
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone halts an American thinker as he steps outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Emersion is the act of emerging, rising out of water or into view.
